content.text:
The faster simple-case closures do not yet tell me whether people have actually resolved their cases. B-O1 is that our incentives reward closures and repeat contacts are not linked to original cases. I propose treating resolution tracking as part of the operational change, while leaving any causal effect unknown.

My staffing constraint is firm: B-O2 permits only one 90-minute assisted-service slot per day, covered by existing staff. I would restrict the fortnight’s assisted route to that capacity and record unmet demand; I cannot promise universal assisted coverage. B-O3 allows me to pause automated closures, but not to change eligibility criteria. I therefore propose pausing automated closure for the bounded pilot workflow while a human-review route is specified with your policy signoff. I cannot authorize the sponsor’s proposed equivalence between completed pages and eligibility approval.

My provisional allocation is two units for the human-review route, two for the assisted slot, two for linked resolution tracking, one for consulting access, and two reserved for a scoped participatory check: nine total. This leaves no separate page-wording allocation. Before committing, we need a review workload existing staff can cover alongside that daily slot, and a check scope we can actually deliver.

Designer, what do the supplied fictional rules require before a case can be approved or closed, and what narrow routing decision can you sign off? I also request access’s advice on evaluating the proposed assisted route and identifying coverage gaps within our fixed capacity; that advice would not itself establish validated access.
